HR@10 against 99 sampled negatives measures ranking within 100 candidates; it is not full-catalog HR@10. Krichene and Rendle show sampled metrics can reverse model comparisons even in expectation. For this benchmark, retain the pinned evaluator and interpret gains specifically under its candidate-sampling protocol. Fixed candidates enable paired comparisons but do not establish robustness to other negative samples. [On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/)

A suitable uncertainty diagnostic is a category-stratified paired user bootstrap: resample the 200 users within each category, preserve each user’s hit indicators for both models, compute category mean differences, then average the four differences equally. Report the observed macro HR@10 difference and a 95% bootstrap interval. This applies the paired-resampling principle documented by [SciPy](https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/generated/scipy.stats.bootstrap.html). Each additional hit changes category HR by 0.005 and the four-category macro average by 0.00125. Such intervals describe user-sampling uncertainty conditional on fitted models and fixed candidates; they exclude training randomness and candidate-resampling uncertainty.

Repeatedly selecting architectures, hyperparameters, or checkpoints on the same small validation set favors configurations benefiting from noise. Cawley and Talbot show this selection bias can rival differences between algorithms. Ordinary paired intervals computed after choosing the winner do not correct adaptive selection. Treat small validation improvements as provisional, record all trials, and reserve generalization claims for the host’s untouched final evaluation; keep hidden test information outside search. [On Over-fitting in Model Selection and Subsequent Selection Bias](https://www.jmlr.org/beta/papers/v11/cawley10a.html)
